title: Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda Cancellation Refund Computation
content:
# Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda Cancellation Refund Computation

Under the Kessler GAP Waiver Addenda, the refund on a holder's cancellation of a waiver is computed from the waiver's own records as follows.

## 1. The computing clause

1.1 The cancellation refund starts from the waiver's price, the retail price charged for the waiver on the installment contract.

1.2 The effective date of the cancellation is the request date the holder signed on the request recorded for the waiver.

1.3 A waiver with no submitted signed cancellation request on file is not cancelled under this rule, and its cancellation refund is 0.00.

1.4 A cancellation whose effective date falls within the free-look period of the waiver's tier (calendar days after the sale date), or whose purchase deal has been unwound, is refunded the full price of the waiver.

1.5 Otherwise the cancellation refund is the waiver's price times the unused share, rounded half up to the cent, less the cancellation fee of the waiver's tier. The unused share is the number of calendar days from the signed request date to the waiver's expiration date divided by the number of calendar days from the sale date to the expiration date.

1.6 A cancellation refund below 0.00 is 0.00.

## 2. Quantities and where they come from

| Quantity | Record it is read from |
|---|---|
| Waiver price | The price recorded on the waiver |
| Signed request date | The request date the holder signed, on the submitted cancellation request recorded for the waiver |
| Sale date and expiration date | The waiver's sale date and expiration date |
| Deal unwound | The status of the waiver's purchase deal |
| Free-look period and cancellation fee | The figures of the waiver's tier in the cancellation and refund terms of the program |

## 3. Order of the figures

The unused share is applied to the waiver's price, that product is rounded half up to the cent, the cancellation fee is then deducted, and a result below 0.00 is set to 0.00. A full-price refund under 1.4 is the waiver's price itself, with no share and no fee.

## 4. Illustration (hypothetical figures)

A waiver priced 643.00 runs 2,191 calendar days from its sale date to its expiration date. The holder signs a cancellation request on a day leaving 1,500 calendar days to expiration, well outside the free-look period, and the deal has not been unwound. The tier's cancellation fee is 50.00.

- Unused share: 1,500 divided by 2,191.
- 643.00 times that share is 440.2099..., rounded half up to 440.21.
- Less the 50.00 fee: the cancellation refund is 390.21.

Had the same request been signed inside the free-look period, the refund would be the full 643.00.

## 5. Points of judgement

- **Is a cancellation refund ever negative?** No; a figure below 0.00 is 0.00.
- **Which date opens the free-look test?** The effective date of the cancellation, counted in calendar days after the sale date (the sale date is day 0); an effective date on the last day of the period is within it, the day after is not.
- **What if no submitted signed request is on file?** The waiver is not cancelled under this rule and the refund is 0.00.
